handback.t:
RESOURCE-REDUCTION (f3) is finished. The smallest viable brain keeps the same router with a smaller state encoding, and the work was done in new bins only. I made no src/ edits and added no crates, downloads or GPU dependency, and I did not run `cargo test`. The VERIFY REQUEST block "### VERIFY REQUEST — RESOURCE-REDUCTION — f3 smallest viable brain" is appended to results/research_board.md and has the rerun commands (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-hr).

**Per-decision cost** (guarded(hebr) is the recommended default; compact is my smaller encoding of the same router; ns is route+feedback on 1 thread, min of 31 reps on a shared box, ±30%):

| Config | 6 agents (sim-fixed) | 32 agents (232 features) |
|---|---|---|
| keyword | 92 ns, 2.4 KB | 113 ns, 9.4 KB |
| warm(hebr) | 1584 ns, 89 KB | 4267 ns, 402 KB |
| guarded(hebr) default | 1034 ns, 16.9 KB, 13 allocs/decision | 3079 ns, 248 KB, 15 allocs |
| coupled | 1574 ns | 5391 ns, and accuracy −0.015 vs guarded |
| +knowledge | 6.0 µs, 520 KB | 12 µs, 1.17 MB |
| compact guarded | 443 ns, 4.4 KB, 0 allocs | 1023 ns (sparse), 61.6 KB (18 KB without its private vocab and keyword map), 0 allocs |

- **Knowledge layer:** it is the only component whose memory and latency grow with traffic: about 260 B per routed task, and ns rises from 3.8 to 8.9 µs over 2000 tasks.
- **Mesh:** the mesh state the CLI/serve actually keeps (team 1, no keyword prior) is cheap, but it loses 0.01–0.13 accuracy to guarded.
- **Pareto:** keyword, coupled (in the sim worlds) and the compact brain are non-dominated. warm, mesh and +knowledge are dominated in every world.

**Smallest viable brain:** 32-bit hashed feature ids (or one shared vocab) with a shared keyword map, u16 weights and baselines, guard counts in 1/1024 units stored as u16, rows dense up to about 8 agents and sparse above. This is the same router logic. In f64 it is decision-for-decision identical to `defaults::recommended_router` (self-tested); the u16/q16 encoding is within noise, as below.

**Accuracy evidence** (tuning only the count scale on seeds 1–8; held-out 31–60, confirm 61–90, plus a 300-seed power run; paired CI vs the unmodified router, equivalence margin 0.003, Holm, 5 worlds):
- **f32:** exactly lossless (difference 0.0000 in every world).
- **u16 weights + f32 counts:** certified equivalent in 5/5 worlds.
- **u16 weights + 1/1024-unit counts:** the 300-seed CI is inside ±0.003 in 5/5 worlds. Holm-TOST is certified in 4/5; in the long-tail world the Holm p is 0.073, so it stays "inconclusive" by my own rule.
- **30-seed splits:** these cannot resolve 0.003 in the 32-agent worlds (CI about ±0.0055), which is why I added the 300-seed run.

**Rejected variants:**
- **u8 weights:** about −0.010 and −0.006 in two sim worlds.
- **bf16:** not certified.
- **Row caps of 25–50%:** −0.03 to −0.095 where every feature row matters.
- **Admission ≥2 plus an LRU cap of 512 rows:** costs at most about 0.004, so use it only as a memory cap for long-tail token streams.

**Brains per GiB** (K real brains built in a fresh child process; live bytes from a counting allocator, commit from the OS):

| World | Default router | Compact brain | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 agents, 32 features | 47.7 k/GiB | 526 k/GiB (2.0 KB each, shared vocab and keywords) | 11× |
| 32 agents, 232 features | 3.9 k/GiB | 55 k/GiB (19.4 KB, sparse) | 14× |
| 32 agents, 1838 features | 509/GiB | 14.8 k/GiB (72.5 KB, sparse hashed), 34.9 k/GiB (30.7 KB, with admission plus a 512-row cap) | 29× / 69× |

Sharing the vocab and keyword map roughly halves a 6-agent brain.

**Throughput with N clients on one shared brain:**
- **One lock:** a single lock gets slower with more threads. The default router goes from 879 k decisions/s (1 thread) to 491 k (8 threads) in the 6-agent world.
- **Per-row locks:** the lock-sharded compact brain reaches 11.6 M/s at 8 threads (3.9× its single-thread rate, 49% of ideal) in the 6-agent world and 4.75 M/s (5.6×) in the 32-agent world.
- **Independent brains:** the upper bound is about 6.5×.
- **Cores:** 8 physical, 16 logical, tested to 8 threads only.

**Finding in the shipped server (`neural-mesh serve` over TCP):**
- **Cost:** it manages 0.8–3.4 k decisions/s with 1–8 clients.
- **Cause:** it writes each reply with `writeln!` on an unbuffered stream, which is 124 write calls and about 929 µs per reply. Formatting the line first or using a BufWriter takes about 9 µs.
- **Ceiling:** with `--stdio` the same server does about 15 k decisions/s, and the single global lock caps it there for any number of clients.
- **Fix:** I did not patch it because serve.rs is read-only for me, but a BufWriter in handle_conn would give about 18× on TCP.

**GPU:** the router and mesh are scalar CPU work at 0.35–3 µs per decision with state in cache, so there is nothing to offload; a kernel launch alone costs more than a whole decision. A GPU could matter only for an optional embedding model feeding the knowledge layer.

**Caveats:**
- **Timing:** ns figures were taken on a shared machine with 1–100% background load. The load before each measurement is recorded in the json.
- **Implementation limits:** the compact brain lives only in the bin. It supports at most 64 agents and neither `task_type` nor team routing.
- **Worlds:** all worlds are synthetic and mine, and the 32-agent worlds follow f2's.
- **f2 overlap:** f2's quantisation results are consistent with mine; the tests differ (f2: warm router, packed persistence; f3: guarded router's resident state), and f3 adds sparse rows, hashed ids and row admission/caps.
